correctness.rationale: The periodic Green kernel is the inverse of a positive second-order precision operator; conditioning on noiseless sites produces independent Dirichlet residual arcs. Solving the Dirichlet forcing and integrating proves the exact f(length), including the singleton case. Rotation-invariant probability enumeration yields every q_k term exactly once. The strict f second derivative gives Jensen equality iff g_(i+k)=g_i; cyclic subgroup theory gives gcd(n,K), including degenerate all-silent laws. Independent Bernoulli probabilities give the exact risk, and uniform cubic Taylor bounds plus geometric domination give the asymptotic factor. A standalone independent matrix-based verifier passes 687 tests across multiple sizes and ranges. Numeric tests are corroboration, not proof.

originality.rationale: No inspected primary theorem states or implies the full circular exact integral risk under arbitrary rotation-invariant correlated erasures, all minimizers via a cyclic gcd, or the Bernoulli large-sample factor. The underlying circular Green covariance, Markov conditioning, Jensen inequality, general quadrature energy identity and open-interval OU optimal sampling are established ingredients rather than new claims. Full texts were compared at the level of object, functional, failure law and quantifiers. Historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Older literature on cyclic Gaussian Markov field sampling or unreliable sensors may have an equivalent convex-gap optimum despite differing terminology; search is not a uniqueness proof.
Full dissertation with OU integral estimation was unavailable; its complete claims were not excluded, although circular correlated erasures are absent from the accessible abstract.

Full text of several related indexed records on circular Matérn precision and covariance may not have been available; title/summary comparisons alone were not used for decisive NOT_COVERING decisions.

value.rationale: A priori site design in the presence of data loss is mathematically motivated for expensive periodic field-integral measurements. The theorem simultaneously identifies a universally optimal robust design, gives a complete and nontrivial classification of all correlated-failure optimizer faces by an arithmetic invariant, and gives an exact asymptotic cost of iid failures (13-fold at 50% delivery). These consequences do not follow automatically from the known no-erasure formula; the nonuniform four-site optimal family marks a meaningful boundary. The result is not claimed to apply to pathwide IMSPE or unrelated kernels.
